commentary:
Risk tone turned constructive overnight, and the story starts in energy: Brent slid below $90, down 2.8%, with WTI off 3.1%, as traders brushed aside Treasury Secretary Bessent's "economic D-Day" sanctions threat against Iran — Qatar's push to mediate the US-Iran dispute took the sting out of the supply-risk premium, with the follow-through hitting gasoil (-1.8%) and dragging TTF gas 2.4% lower. That crude retreat did the heavy lifting elsewhere: falling oil eased the inflation math, bond yields dropped, and equities rallied — Treasuries bid across the curve with the long bond up 0.4%, Bunds and gilts firmer, and Nasdaq futures up 0.9% as chipmakers rebounded ahead of Nvidia earnings and this week's Jackson Hole gathering, where markets are hunting for clear Fed guidance before PCE data.

The other macro thread is Bessent's move to more than double long-dated Treasury buybacks — read by many as yield-curve management by another name and, per some strategists, just another route to a weaker dollar. Prediction markets remain sceptical it caps yields into 2026, and the "debasement trade" is back: gold is holding near $4,700 with crypto extending gains, even as the softer risk-off tone knocked platinum and palladium 1.5-2.4% lower. Ags were broadly heavy — wheat down 2-2.6%, sugar, cotton and robusta all off more than 1% — consistent with the deflating commodity complex.

Watch Jackson Hole rhetoric, PCE, and whether Iran mediation headlines keep crude — and with it the rates bid — moving in tandem.
